accuracy.evidence: Every target was multiplied out by hand: x²+5x+6=(x+2)(x+3), x²+7x+12=(x+3)(x+4), x²+x−6=(x−2)(x+3), x²−7x+10=(x−2)(x−5), x²−9=(x+3)(x−3), worked example x²−2x−15=(x+3)(x−5).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the classic slips: copying b and c straight into the brackets, picking a pair with the right product but wrong sum, and flipping both signs when c is negative or b is negative.

lab_distinct.evidence: Algebra-tile rectangle: x² tile, p strips on top, q strips down the side and a p×q corner block of unit tiles, sized by dragging the corner handle; shingle similarity tops out at 2.7%.

lab_teaches.evidence: Area equals the trinomial, so the learner sees the corner block count is c and the strip total is b; negative strips turn pink and make the corner negative when exactly one side is negative.

predictions.evidence: Five predicts with tempting wrong options: (x+5)(x+6) copies b and c, 2 and 6 has the right product only, (x+2)(x−3) flips signs, and x²−9 offers 'no x term so no' and (x−3)(x−3); the rectangle disproves each.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Probe on iPhone 13: 2,6 gave right product wrong sum; −3,−4 gave both signs flipped; 5,2 gave right sum wrong product; 5,3 for −15 explained a negative c needs one negative; plus Show me walk.

readability.evidence: Flesch–Kincaid grade 3.5 for kid text and 5.9 for adult text, well inside the validator limits; one rule per paragraph.

no_filler.evidence: Filler regex passes and lesson text overlap with existing lessons is 0%; every paragraph carries the product-and-sum rule, a sign rule or the x²−2x−15 worked example.

mobile.evidence: Real CDP touch drag of the corner handle on iPhone 13 completed step 0; phone sweep reported 0 findings and screenshots show tiles unclipped with edge labels tappable.

accessibility.evidence: axe-core clean in dark and light themes on desktop and iPhone; every gesture has button equivalents (Top/Side ±1, flip sign) and the canvas carries an aria-label with live status text.
